steps.name: Fix Rect.contains to inclusive boundary and implement hitTestButton traversal
steps.description: Two inseparable tasks: (1) fix Rect.contains in LayoutTypes.swift to use <= instead of < on both axes (ODQ-01 prerequisite for AC-06), then (2) implement the depth-first hitTestButton free function in HitTest.swift replacing the nil-returning scaffold. The traversal mirrors layoutNode cast priority: AnyButton -> ContainerView -> ZStackView -> HasFrameSize -> AnyPaddingModifier -> leaf.
steps.criteria: All 13 HitTestButtonTests pass; all 101 pre-existing tests remain green; Rect.contains uses inclusive boundary (<=); hitTestButton is a public free function with no Foundation import.
acceptance_criteria: hitTestButton(view:node:at:) returns the traversal-order index of the first AnyButton whose LayoutNode.frame contains point
Returns nil when no AnyButton frame contains the point
Traversal is depth-first matching view-tree construction order
Works when buttons are nested inside VStack, HStack, FrameModifier containers
Point on frame boundary (top-left and bottom-right corners) counts as contained
Traversal never invokes any button's anyAction closure
All 101 existing tests remain green after Rect.contains fix
All 13 HitTestButtonTests pass (12 enabled after scaffold replacement)
steps.scenario_name: Walking skeleton — cursor over single button returns its index
steps.implementation_notes: 1. Fix Rect.contains: change both < to <= on lines 40-41 of LayoutTypes.swift. Run full test suite — all 101 existing tests must stay green. 2. Replace HitTest.swift scaffold body with recursive depth-first traversal. Private helper hitTestNode(_:_:at:index:) takes inout Int counter incremented only on AnyButton casts. 3. Enable all .disabled tests in HitTestButtonTests.swift one at a time as each scenario goes GREEN. The two ODQ-01 boundary tests can be enabled after step 1.
